relatedSnapshot.title: Promo codes still fail at checkout: single-plan Autumn checkout sends promo code via legacy reward field
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Users entering a discount code during a single-plan upgrade still get a generic "Something went wrong" at checkout, because that checkout path sends the code to Autumn through a legacy field Autumn no longer accepts.

## Problem

When a user enters an Autumn discount code and submits, `billing.createCheckout` fails and the UI shows "Something went wrong", blocking the upgrade.

## Root cause

In `apps/web/lib/billing/providers/autumn/client.ts`, `createSubscriptionCheckout` passes `input.promoCode` to `autumn.attach()` through the legacy `reward` field. Autumn rejects Stripe/Autumn promotion codes sent this way with "Reward <CODE> not found", and the `billing.createCheckout` catch block converts that to a generic `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` that tRPC masks as "Something went wrong". The sibling `createMultiAttachCheckout` already sends the code correctly via `discounts: [{ promotion_code }]` through `v2.multiAttach`, so the fix pattern exists; the single-plan attach path was never migrated.

## Blast radius

9 organizations / 9 users, ~66 "Reward ... not found" checkout errors over the last 30 days (codes such as AIAUTO100 and <promo-code>), counted from the Axiom `acquisity` dataset (`message contains "attaching subscription"`, grouped by the Autumn error message) on 2026-09-03.

## Prior art

Recurrence of the same root cause as [ENG-9213] (legacy `reward` field); that fix covered the multi-attach path but not the single-plan `createSubscriptionCheckout` path.

## Proposed fix

Migrate `createSubscriptionCheckout` off the legacy `reward` field to Autumn's current discount shape (`discounts: [{ promotion_code }]`), matching `createMultiAttachCheckout`, and surface a promo-code-specific error instead of the generic "Something went wrong".

## Done when

* Entering a valid Autumn promo code on a single-plan upgrade creates the checkout with the discount applied.
* An invalid/expired promo code shows a clear promo-code error, not "Something went wrong".
* A regression test proves the attach payload sends the promo code via the discount field, not `reward`.
